thread.title: UPDATE: Apple has big spending plans, but the 'smart money' isn't buying tech stocks

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Apple has big spending plans, but the 'smart money' isn't buying tech stocks
text:
By Nigam Arora
Nigam Arora says investors ought to sell into strength and buy the dips
Apple is the first big tech company to hand President Trump a win.
Apple (AAPL) in a press release Wednesday, said it will pay $38 billion in repatriation taxes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-didnt-say-it-was-hiring-20000-new-workers-nor-bringing-back-its-overseas-cash-2018-01-17), spend $30 billion in capital expenditures over the next five years and help create 20,000 new jobs inside and outside the company.
Trump sent out a tweet (https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/953771038114045954) praising the Cupertino, Calif.-based maker of the iPhone.
Apple is borrowing a page from Amazon's (AMZN) playbook and plans to build a new campus (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazoncoms-hq2-finalists-include-new-york-chicago-la-atlanta-boston-dallas-washington-2018-01-18). Could other tech companies be far behind? Such news may move those companies' stocks.
Read:What Amazon's new headquarters means for homeowners and renters in the chosen city (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/what-amazons-hq2-means-for-homeowners-home-buyers-and-renters-in-the-chosen-city-2017-10-20)
But how much of the upcoming news is already discounted? What does it all mean for investors? To find out, investors can gain an edge by looking at money flows. Let us explore with the help of a chart.
Chart
Please click here (https://thearorareport.com/chart-money-flows-popular-tech-stocks-01182018) for a chart showing money flows in popular tech stocks. In addition to Apple and Amazon, the chart shows money flows in FAANG and other popular tech stocks.
Please observe the following from the chart:
-- The momo (momentum) crowd is aggressively buying tech stocks.
-- Short squeezes are adding to the buying. In a short squeeze, short-sellers (who bet on declines) buy stocks to cover to cut their losses. That adds fuel to the fire.
-- The "smart money" of professional investors is not overly enthusiastic.

Interpretation of the smart money's moves
The momo crowd typically buys because the price is going up. It is not known for its strength in analysis.
The smart money takes a portfolio approach. The run in tech stocks has produced outsized positions in many portfolios. From a risk perspective, it does not make sense to add to positions that are already disproportionately large. As a matter of fact, it makes sense to trim them into the strength.
As an example, in The Arora Report portfolio, Apple is a long position from a price of $18.71. With Apple trading around $179, the original position is now 956% of the original position.
As another example, Facebook (FB) was bought by The Arora Report at $49.92. With Facebook trading around $177, the position has become disproportionately big too.
What to do now
Broadly speaking, investors fall into two categories: Those in these stocks and those not in these stocks.
Those in these positions may consider continuing to hold but review them to make sure they have not become disproportionately large. If they have, it is better to start scaling out in small tranches as opposed to panicking and selling into weakness. To learn why tranching is important, please see "The average investor is making a classic mistake as the Dow marches to 30,000 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-average-investor-is-making-a-classic-mistake-as-the-dow-marches-to-30000-2018-01-16)." Please also read: "Apple's stock could double on the 'mother of all artificial-intelligence projects (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-stock-could-double-on-the-mother-of-all-artificial-intelligence-projects-2017-08-02).' "
At The Arora Report, we recognize that all investors are different. For this reason, we provide four ways to invest: Good Way, Better Way, Best Way and Your Way to meet individual styles and needs. For those not in these stocks and following the Good Way, our "buy now" rating is a "yes" for Apple, Facebook, Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOGL) and Alibaba (BABA). For those following the Best Way and not in these stocks, it is prudent to wait for dips into the buy zones.
